# Two branches rename the same user to different names. Rename is single-valued,
# so ours wins and theirs' rename is dropped (with a warning).

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Base: bob in dev.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: rename bob -> dave.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user rename bob dave
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob -> dave'

# THEIRS: rename bob -> erin.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user rename bob erin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: bob -> erin'

# Merge: the driver merges the log and reports a conflict (exit 1) so git stops.
# NOTE: git additionally raises a rename/rename tree conflict on the signkey file
# (bob.age -> dave.age vs erin.age) - see the report; reconciling that from the
# log is still open.
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stdout 'merged it automatically'

# ours' rename to dave is applied; theirs' rename is dropped and the merge entry
# records that decision (so "erin" appears only in the drop record, not as a
# live rename).
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"new_name": "dave"'
stdout 'rename source bob'
! stdout '"new_name": "erin"'
